arxiv-2307-03733.title: “How Did They Come Across?” Lessons Learned from Continuous Affective Ratings
arxiv-2307-03733.creator: Maria Teresa Parreira 1 , Michael J. Sack 1 , Hifza Javed 2 , Nawid Jamali 2 , and Malte Jung 1
arxiv-2307-03733.description: Abstract Social distance, or perception of the other, is recognized as a dynamic dimension of an interaction, but yet to be widely explored or understood. Through CORAE, a novel web-based open-source tool for COntinuous Retrospective Affect Evaluation , we collected retrospective ratings of interpersonal perceptions between 12 participant dyads.

arxiv-2309-02633.title: Vortex Creep Heating vs. Dark Matter Heating in Neutron Stars
arxiv-2309-02633.creator: Motoko Fujiwara, Koichi Hamaguchi, Natsumi Nagata, Maura E. Ramirez-Quezada
arxiv-2309-02633.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Motoko Fujiwara, Koichi Hamaguchi, Natsumi Nagata, Maura E. Ramirez-Quezada. Dark matter particles captured in neutron stars deposit their energy as heat. This DM heating effect can be observed only if it dominates over other internal heating effects in NSs. In this work, as an example of such an internal heating source, we consider the frictional heating caused by the creep motion of neutron superfluid vortex lines in the NS crust.

arxiv-2508-05330.creator: Susmita Chowdhury, Rachana Gupta, Najnin Bano, Yogesh Kumar, Shashi Prakash, Dinesh Kumar Shukla, Vasant G. Sathe, Mukul Gupta

arxiv-2510-25832.title: The dark dimension, proton decay, and the length of the M-theory interval
arxiv-2510-25832.creator: Mario Reig, and Ignacio Ruiz
arxiv-2510-25832.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mario Reig, and Ignacio Ruiz. The existence of a large extra dimension in which only gravity propagates would have spectacular consequences for cosmology and laboratory experiments. In the strong coupling limit of the E 8 × E 8 E_{8}\times E_{8} heterotic string theory, the gauge and matter fields live at the end of the eleventh dimension, which becomes a natural candidate for a micron-size dark dimension .

arxiv-2601-01941.title: Settling of chiral particles in a turbulent flow
arxiv-2601-01941.creator: Mees M. Flapper 1, John E. Sader 2, Detlef Lohse 1,3, Sander G. Huisman 1
arxiv-2601-01941.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Mees M. Flapper 1, John E. Sader 2, Detlef Lohse 1,3, Sander G. Huisman 1. Chiral particles are experimentally investigated while settling in water with various turbulence intensity levels. The locations and orientations of the particles are tracked over time, allowing the close investigation of the particles’ settling dynamics. The generated turbulent flow is measured using laser Doppler anemometry (LDA), and the turbulence strength varies between experiments in the range 0 ≤ Re λ ≤ 250 0\leq\text{Re}_{\lambda}\leq 250 .

plos-pone-0001191.creator: Catherine Tempel-Brami, Iddo Pinkas, Avigdor Scherz et al.
plos-pone-0001191.description: PLOS ONE research article. In this study, we show how light can be absorbed by the body of a living rat due to an injected pigment circulating in the blood stream. This process is then physiologically translated in the tissue into a chemical signature that can be perceived as an image by magnetic resonance

plos-pone-0008725.title: Therapeutic Efficacy and Immunological Response of CCL5 Antagonists in Models of Contact Skin Reaction
plos-pone-0008725.creator: Miriam Canavese, Fiorella Altruda, Lorenzo Silengo
plos-pone-0008725.description: PLOS ONE research article. Skin-infiltrating T-cells play a predominant role in allergic and inflammatory skin diseases such as atopic dermatitis, psoriasis and allergic contact dermatitis. These T-cells are attracted by several chemotactic factors including the chemokine CCL5/RANTES, a CC chemokine induci

pmc-10911229.title: Upstream mobility and swarming of light activated micromotors†
pmc-10911229.creator: Bingzhi Wu, David P. Rivas, Sambeeta Das
pmc-10911229.description: Micromotors have been proposed for applications such as targeted drug delivery, thrombolysis, or sensing. However, single micrormotors are limited in the amount of payload they can deliver or force they can exert. Swarms of micromotors can overcome many of these challenges, however creating and controlling such swarms presents many challenges of its own.

pmc-11404571.title: CircBIRC6 affects prostate cancer progression by regulating miR-574-5p and DNAJB1
pmc-11404571.creator: Bin Zhao, Jinye Yang, Fengming Ran, Yuanlong Shi, Libo Yang, Yuanpeng Duan, Zhiyu Shi, Xin Li, Jianpeng Zhang, Zhiyao Li, Jiansong Wang
pmc-11404571.description: BackgroundProstate cancer (PCa) is among the three main types of cancer. Although prostate-specific antigen (PSA) is routinely tested, it has disadvantages, such as poor prognostic ability. Therefore, finding more PCa markers and therapeutic targets remains a subject of study. CircRNAs have been found to have regulatory roles in various diseases, such as diabetes, Central Nervous System (CNS) neuropathy, etc.

pmc-11442663.title: Surface protein distribution in Group B Streptococcus isolates from South Africa and identifying vaccine targets through in silico analysis
pmc-11442663.creator: Vicky Gent, Ying-Jie Lu, Sindiswa Lukhele, Nisha Dhar, Ziyaad Dangor, Nancy Hosken, Richard Malley, Shabir A Madhi, Gaurav Kwatra
pmc-11442663.description: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) is a major cause of pneumonia, sepsis, and meningitis in infants younger than 3 months of age. Furthermore, GBS infection in pregnant women is associated with stillbirths and pre-term delivery. It also causes disease in immunocompromised adults and the elderly, but the highest incidence of the disease occurs in neonates and young infants.

pmc-11503353.title: “This Is Me” an Awareness-Raising and Anti-Stigma Program for Undergraduate Nursing Students: A Pre-Post Intervention Study
pmc-11503353.creator: Olga Valentim, Tânia Correia, Lídia Moutinho, Paulo Seabra, Ana Querido, Carlos Laranjeira, Richard Gray
pmc-11503353.description: Background: Stigma education for nursing students has focused solely on stigma reduction, with studies showing temporary improvements in attitudes. However, nursing education research should also emphasize the importance of critical reflection and self-reflection to enhance attitudes, beliefs, topic comprehension, and learning satisfaction.

pmc-12088217.title: Alternative Methods of Fixation for Anterior Tibialis Transfer in Residual Clubfoot Deformity
pmc-12088217.creator: Spencer Wilson, Laura L. Bellaire, Kenneth J. Noonan
pmc-12088217.description: The preferred treatment for congenital clubfoot is the Ponseti method, which involves weekly manipulation and casting followed by tendoachilles tenotomy and abduction bracing. Depending on patient age and deformity location, 5%–35% of patients experience recurrent deformities and require additional treatment, including casting or surgery.

pmc-12583916.title: Neural network dynamics underlying the bottom-up perception and top-down regulation processes of empathy
pmc-12583916.creator: Xiao Wu, Ya-Zhuo Kong, Li Hu
pmc-12583916.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Contemporary theoretical models of empathy propose that it involves both bottom-up perception and top-down regulation processes. Although previous studies have explored brain regions involved in empathy, direct evidence for a hierarchical organization in empathy processing remains limited. In this functional magnetic resonance imaging study, we sought to address this gap by using positive, negative, and neutral stimuli to explore whether shared or valence-specific processing underlies positive and negative empathy.

pmc-12629878.title: Evaluating Circulating Tumor DNA Clearance as an Early Intermediate End Point Predicting Clinical Benefit in Metastatic Nonsquamous NSCLC After First-Line Chemoimmunotherapy
pmc-12629878.creator: Min Yuan, Haolun Ding, Weiwei Zhuang, Yaning Yang, Xu Steven Xu
pmc-12629878.description: IntroductionIn the first-line (1L) NSCLC setting, overall survival (OS) as a trial end point is increasingly challenging due to longer survival and confounding from novel later-line therapies. This study aims to evaluate whether circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) clearance (alone or with radiographic response) is a reliable early surrogate end point for progression-free survival (PFS) and OS in 1L NSCLC studies.

pmc-12663313.title: Experimental study on the performance and mechanism of high-pressure abrasive water jet cutting GFRP bars reinforced concrete structures
pmc-12663313.creator: Jingwei Xu, Hu Yu, Chuang Huang, Biao Li, Bin Liu, Jian Qiu, Jiwen Wang
pmc-12663313.description: Abrasive water jet (AWJ) cutting technology is considered an effective method to assist tunnel boring machines in efficiently breaking glass fiber reinforced polymer (GFRP) bar reinforced concrete structures. However, systematic investigations on the coupled cutting behavior of GFRP bars and concrete remain limited.

pmc-12764698.title: The effects of adding decitabine to conditioning regimen for patients with acute myeloid leukemia or myelodysplastic syndrome undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12764698.creator: Chengxin Luo, Jianmin Zhang, Xiangtao Huang, Guixian Wu, Yarui Huang, Yaqun Ding, Zhen Huang, Qiuyue Song, Jieping Chen, Xi Li, Shuangnian Xu
pmc-12764698.description: Decitabine shows favorable efficacy in induction and maintenance therapy for patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), but its role in pre-transplant conditioning still has not been established. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative studies investigating the effects of adding decitabine to conditioning regimens in AML/MDS patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

pmc-13150917.title: Mentoring Trauma Nurses: A Global Perspective on Leadership and Resilience in Conflict Zones
pmc-13150917.creator: Kathleen Martin, Zakk Arciaga
pmc-13150917.description: Kathleen Martin (KM) is an internationally renowned trauma nurse, mentor, and humanitarian whose career has impacted trauma nurses. As the keynote speaker for this year’s Sharon M Henry Maryland Committee on Trauma State-of-the-Art Lecture, no one is better qualified to illuminate the vital—but too often overlooked—role of trauma nursing in austere and conflict-affected settings than KM.

pmc-13217513.title: A cohort study on inflammatory response and coagulation function changes in women with silver clip or silk ligation sterilisation
pmc-13217513.creator: Yuan Wang, Yunfeng Li, Mengdi Wang, Yumei Ma, Jie Yang, Lijuan Zhang
pmc-13217513.description: BackgroundTo investigate the long-term systemic effects of tubal sterilisation using the silver clip technique, a commonly used yet understudied permanent contraceptive method, by evaluating its impact on inflammatory responses and coagulation function.DiscussionA multicentre ambispective cohort study will be conducted in ten hospitals.

pmc-13344378.title: Risk factors for unplanned cesarean delivery among pregnant individuals with pre‐existing diabetes
pmc-13344378.creator: Marie‐Julie Trahan, Qi Yan, Meghan Angley, Kim A Boggess, Jerrie S Refuerzo, Kacey Y Eichelberger, Gladys A Ramos, Celeste Durnwald, Kjersti M Aagaard, Kedra Wallace, Christina Scifres, Todd Rosen, Sherri Longo, Noelia Zork
pmc-13344378.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundDiabetes in pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery, including unplanned or emergency cesarean delivery. It is unclear which risk factors confer increased risk of cesarean among pregnancies with Type 2 diabetes or early gestational diabetes.

pmc-13416866.title: Occurrence, Sources, and Ecological Risks of Organochlorine Pesticides in Sediments of Typical Plateau Lakes, Southwest China
pmc-13416866.creator: Zhonghong Zhao, Li Bao, Min Ye, Naiming Zhang
pmc-13416866.description: This study investigated the contamination characteristics, sources, and ecological risks of organochlorine pesticides (OCPs) in surface sediments from three plateau lakes in southwestern China (Qilu Lake, Dianchi Lake, and Yangzonghai Lake). Significant differences in OCP pollution levels were observed among the three lakes.

pmc-13583786.title: Benefits of childhood vaccines in ecological studies focusing on Germany: a scoping review protocol
pmc-13583786.creator: Tristan Nolting, David D Martin
pmc-13583786.description: IntroductionGeneral statements that vaccinations are among the most important preventive measures in medicine are common in public health guidance. While the efficacy of individual vaccines is well established through randomised controlled trials and observational studies, ecological studies at the population level can provide complementary insights into the relative historical contributions of different childhood vaccinations to reductions in morbidity and mortality.

pmc-13593541.creator: Henry Zheng, Lukasz Cerbin, Nicholas Palmeri, Madison Munger, Sri Sundaram, Daniel Alyesh

pmc-13644777.title: Investigating mechanisms and monitoring outcomes in functional neurological disorder: the unrealized potential of digital remote monitoring technologies
pmc-13644777.creator: Susannah Pick, Matthew Hotopf
pmc-13644777.description: Functional neurological disorder (FND) is characterized by involuntary, distressing neurological symptoms that are distinguishable from other neurological diagnoses in presentation, aetiology and mechanisms. Significant disability, impaired quality-of-life and substantial healthcare resource utilization often result from the disorder, yet its underlying mechanisms have not been proven empirically. Importantly, long-term clinical trajectories and predictive markers have been understudied in FND cohorts.
